svg.title: HybridGuard: associated observation surfaces and optional C1 relation
svg.desc: A cooperating Android app contains Native APIs and a WebView Host; App Web JavaScript is nested in the Host. Native-Web memory and timezone comparisons are integrated. Host-Web geometry is a standalone study outside Integrated App and its candidate pool. The dotted Native-Host link denotes shared context only. Schema counts are Native 84, Host 26, App Web 67 and external Browser 67; selected detectors use subsets. The external Browser is a separate Web execution; Chrome 133 and 134 identify the evaluated implementation. A thin leader enlarges the App Web record into the C1 panel, not an additional execution. Illustrative App Web and Browser timezone offsets are -480 and -540 minutes under UTC-minus-local. Both show field status observed and quality observed_value. C1 requires valid association and finite numeric non-Boolean offsets. The illustrated inequality yields T, the C1 condition outcome, not the whole detector result. Equal usable offsets yield F; unusable evidence yields U; invalid association yields FAILED. C1 has no timestamp gate. Connectors denote comparison, containment, or record excerpts, not inter-application communication, synchronized sampling, or attestation. No surface is trusted ground truth. Android and Chrome retain their source identity assets. Six app marks are illustrative identities reused from Figure 2; they do not expand the evaluated app list. The WebView and technical pictograms are original editable vector drawings. The page offsets decorate record cards and do not add executions. Clock hands schematically indicate different effective offsets, not collection times. The red mismatch icon denotes the illustrated C1 condition outcome, not a detector-wide alert. Visual revision: three same-style observation cards and three equal-width, equal-head bidirectional arrows. Blue is integrated Native/Web consistency, ochre dashed is standalone Host/Web geometry, and gray dotted is shared context only, not a detector rule. App Web remains in the WebView context.

g.inkscape:label: C1 comparison — original geometry
g.text: Equal → F · Unusable → U · Invalid link → FAILED

svg.text: Counts describe schemas, not selected inputs. No surface is trusted ground truth.
